Overview

This is the example threat model AWS ships with Threat Composer, for a retrieval-augmented chatbot on Amazon Bedrock. One JSON workspace holds the application description, a reference architecture and a data-flow model. The architecture covers data preparation with S3, Lambda and Titan embeddings; a front end behind Cognito, WAF and a load balancer; OpenSearch Serverless as the vector store; and Bedrock with Guardrails. The data-flow model has nine entities, nine flows (DF1 to DF9, each listing the assets it carries) and six trust boundaries (TB1 to TB6). On top of that sit 13 assumptions, 37 threat statements and 84 mitigations. Each threat is written in Threat Composer's grammar (source, prerequisites, action, impact, impacted goal and assets) and tagged with an OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 category, STRIDE letters and a priority. Every threat links to at least one mitigation, and 95 further links tie assumptions to threats and mitigations. The disclaimer presents it as an informational starting point: a hypothetical operator ranks confidentiality of the retrieval data first, integrity of answers second and availability last, and readers should set their own priorities.

Limits

  • An example, by its own disclaimer. It is informational, provided as is, a proof of concept for one reference architecture, and not a complete end-to-end solution.
  • Nothing is validated. All 37 threats are in the identified state and all 84 mitigations in the identified state; none is marked resolved or tested.
  • Assets are free text. The impacted assets have no controlled vocabulary, as RPT-0014's TM-026 entry also notes.
  • Some tags look misassigned. T-14, a supplier providing poisoned training data, carries STRIDE E and R rather than T, and T-15, a deprecated inference API, carries E and S. The text has small errors ("can can", "egitimate", "leads to leads to"), and the numbering skips T-8 and T-27.
  • Specific to AWS services. Bedrock, OpenSearch Serverless, Cognito and the rest are named throughout; mapping the model to another stack is left to the reader.
  • A file that changes. Earlier versions differ, for example before the 2025-04-02 update; the digest pins this content.
